programme: HLF, CBFA2T3, PAX5 and CEBPE are canonical hematopoietic lineage-commitment transcription factors that sit at the myeloid-versus-lymphoid branch point of blood cell production: HLF maintains HSC/progenitor output, CBFA2T3 (ETO2) acts as a RUNX1-complex corepressor shaping that branch, PAX5 commits and locks progenitors into the B-lymphoid programme (CD19, CD79A, BLNK, VPREB1, EBF1 among its targets) while actively repressing myeloid genes, and CEBPE drives terminal granulocyte differentiation (its targets ELANE, MPO, CTSG, S100A8, S100A9 are the classic neutrophil/azurophilic-granule and calprotectin gene set). Recurring together in blood-derived networks, they read as a signature of a shifted myeloid:lymphoid output ratio rather than four independent hits.
role_in_a: In psoriasis, neutrophil-driven inflammation is a defining feature of lesional and circulating disease activity (Munro's-microabscess neutrophils, S100A8/S100A9 calprotectin as an established severity marker), which is exactly the CEBPE-driven granulocyte output this module encodes; a concordant pull toward CEBPE/HLF myeloid output and away from the PAX5 B-lymphoid programme is consistent with that known neutrophil skew.
role_in_b: In ischemic stroke, an acute-phase rise in neutrophils and fall in lymphocytes (the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, a well-established prognostic marker) is one of the best-documented peripheral-blood correlates of outcome; the same CEBPE/HLF-up, PAX5-down pattern would be the transcriptional substrate of that shift, and 37282471 independently reports an altered, more phagocytic circulating B-cell phenotype after stroke, i.e. a change in the PAX5-governed compartment.
shared_axis: Both conditions are associated with a myeloid-skewed, lymphoid-suppressed circulating leukocyte profile — chronic in psoriasis, acute in stroke — so blood-sampled networks in each disease would independently recover the same hematopoietic lineage-commitment factors (HLF/CBFA2T3 setting progenitor output, CEBPE driving the granulocyte arm, PAX5 marking the suppressed lymphoid arm) even without a documented psoriasis–stroke comorbidity mechanism linking them directly.
reasoning: The module is textbook-nameable and mid-tier in recurrence (11–12/24, well below SMARCA5's 16/24 and ARNT's 14/24, neither of which fits this or any other coherent story here), so this is a real but not dominant signal. Only PAX5 has an on-topic retrieved paper placing it in stroke, and even that is interpretive; HLF's retrieved papers are entirely name-confounded (hawthorn leaf flavonoids/healthy lifestyle factors), CBFA2T3's are off-topic (cardiovascular aging, sickle cell), and CEBPE's are off-topic (heatstroke, leukemia blood-trait GWAS) — three of four carrying factors have no usable retrieved evidence, so the account leans on established disease physiology (NLR in stroke, calprotectin/neutrophils in psoriasis) rather than on what was actually retrieved.
support: PMID 37282471 — reports a distinct, more phagocytic/chemotactic circulating B-cell phenotype after ischemic stroke, consistent with a perturbation of the PAX5-governed B-lymphoid compartment in this disease. No usable PMIDs were retrieved for HLF, CBFA2T3, or CEBPE in either disease: the HLF hits are confounded with 'hawthorn leaf flavonoids'/'healthy lifestyle factors', and the CBFA2T3/CEBPE hits (cardiovascular aging genetics, sickle cell anemia, heatstroke, leukemia blood-trait loci) do not address stroke or psoriasis directly.
how_to_falsify: In matched blood samples from psoriasis patients, stroke patients, and healthy controls, quantify the granulocyte fraction/CEBPE-target expression (S100A8, S100A9, ELANE, MPO) against the B-cell fraction/PAX5-target expression (CD19, CD79A, BLNK) by flow cytometry or scRNA-seq. The account predicts a concordant shift toward the myeloid arm and away from the PAX5 B-lymphoid arm in both diseases relative to controls; if the neutrophil:B-cell ratio and its transcriptional markers do not move together in psoriasis and stroke — or move in opposite directions — the shared-axis claim is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (stroke) against skin/blood (psoriasis), and both diseases had zero Open Targets association records for any of the four carrying factors, so nothing here is corroborated by an independent association database. Concordance is drawn from only 4 independent cohort pairs generating 24 patient-group comparisons, so the 11–12/24 recurrence for these factors reflects a small number of truly independent replicates, not 24 independent tests. Classic generic immune/myeloid master regulators (STAT2, STAT5B, TBX21, BCL6, EPAS1, SPIB, DNMT1) were already stripped out as tissue-generic before ranking, which is why this account had to be built from lineage-commitment factors rather than the more obvious inflammatory TFs — a sign the remaining signal is somewhat specific, but also a reminder that the more familiar immune story was deliberately excluded, not overlooked. The two strongest-recurring factors overall, SMARCA5 and ARNT, do not fit this or any other module offered here and are left unexplained; ARNT's retrieved 'stroke' literature in particular appears to be confounded with its paralog ARNTL/BMAL1 (circadian biology), not ARNT itself.
